ctx.x: And we weren't bothering anybody, weren't breaking any laws, and I just don't understand it. It was a real drag for us because we were known coast to coast on this thing, because when bands would come in town, they'd say, "Hey, where is this (unintelligible) Clef Club club that we've been hearing about, you know, so and so? Well, it doesn't start until 2:00 o'clock in the morning," you know. The guys said, "We'll be there," you know, and all the bands that would play these one nighters that would come in town.…

Why, Harry James' band, with Ernie Andrews, the great singer -- all these guys would come up and play, sit in and jam. Brother Jack McDuff with was the great drummer that eventually stayed in Denver. After he left McDuff, Joe Dukes,
and he was with the house band, and we had a great bandleader right here in Denver now, Towles. that's like (unintelligible), Billy Tells. He had that band.
